newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FLOODS CLAIM 15 LIVES, THOUSANDS EVACUATED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FLOODS CLAIM 15 LIVES, THOUSANDS EVACUATED.

text.p: Floods in southern Poland following five days of heavy rain have so far claimed at least 15 lives and forced 20,000 to leave their homes, the spokesman for the national civil defence said on Thursday.

Captain Leszek Korpus told Reuters more people would be forced to evacuate as the flood wave on the Oder river hit the south-western city of Opole inundating its old town and cutting off the left bank part of the town.
"So far we have confirmed 15 drownings. More than 20,000 people have been evacuated but as the flood wave hits Opole, we can expect more will be forced to leave homes," Korpus said.
Of the 15 dead, seven drowned in the Walbrzych province, three in Bielsko-Biala area, two in Opole and one in Nowy Sacz, Katowice and Jelenia Gora each over the last five days.
Korpus said already 310,000 hectares of land were under water, including 10 towns and seven villages.

"The situation has improved in the Legnica area and in Jelenia Gora, but forecasts are not optimistic as the situation deteriorates in Katowice, Opole and other towns on the Oder river -- Brzeg and Wroclaw are under threat," he said.
Korpus said more than 15,000 firefighters, soldiers, border guards and policemen took part in the rescue efforts, helped by 20 helicopters and 160 boats.

No official estimates of the size of the damange are available but the government has already said it had no money to reimburse the victims of the flood who had not insured themselves drawing heavy criticism from the opposition just two months before parliamentary elections.
